title: Build a decision memo system
description: A system that turns a hard decision into a one-page memo with options, evidence, and a recommendation before you decide.

push.title: Push
push.content: Sending your local commits up to GitHub so the online repo matches your computer. When Claude says it's 'pushing to GitHub,' it's uploading your latest changes so they're saved in the cloud and visible to others.

agent.title: Agent
agent.content: An AI that works independently to complete a goal — planning steps, picking tools, running them, and deciding what to do next without you prompting it at every step. Unlike a chatbot, an agent takes action.

model.title: Model
model.content: A specific trained version of an AI. Claude has several models (like Opus, Sonnet, Haiku) that differ in capability and speed. Larger models are smarter but slower; smaller ones are faster and cheaper.

skill.title: Skill
skill.content: A plain-text file with instructions for a specific repeatable workflow. Save it once, then trigger it with a slash command like /research-competitive. Same steps and output format every time — like a macro for Claude.

slack.title: Slack
slack.content: The team messaging app most companies run on. In Level 2, students connect Slack to their AI tools to trigger workflows from messages, post AI-generated updates to channels, or summarize threads automatically.

claude.title: Claude
claude.content: The AI made by Anthropic. Available as a chat tool at claude.ai, as a desktop app (Claude Desktop), and as a terminal tool (Claude Code). The different interfaces are suited for different types of work.

commit.title: Commit
commit.content: A saved snapshot of your files at a specific moment in time — like 'Save As' with a label. Used in Git. If something breaks, you can go back to a previous commit.

notion.title: Notion
notion.content: An all-in-one workspace for docs, wikis, databases, and project tracking. Used heavily across the AI Builder program as a destination for AI-generated content and as a connected app in Level 2 automations.

prompt.title: Prompt
prompt.content: The instruction or message you give to an AI. The quality of your prompt directly shapes the quality of the output. Writing better prompts is one of the highest-leverage skills in this program.

rubric.title: Rubric
rubric.content: The written definition of what a good output looks like, in 3–5 scoreable dimensions. Evals grade against a rubric; without one, 'is this good?' is a vibe, not a measurement.

chatgpt.title: ChatGPT
chatgpt.content: OpenAI's chat assistant. The most widely known AI tool — works similarly to Claude but with different strengths and weaknesses. Useful to have access to for cross-checking outputs or trying alternate models.

automation.title: Automation
automation.content: Having Claude run tasks automatically on a schedule or trigger — without you manually starting them each time. For example, checking your inbox every morning and summarizing it to Slack.

tool-connectors.title: Tool Connectors
tool-connectors.content: Integrations that let Claude read from and write to apps you use (Gmail, Slack, Google Calendar, Notion, HubSpot, etc.). Set up once in Customize → Connectors. Each connector opens up a new category of tasks Claude can automate.

personal-knowledge-base.title: Personal Knowledge Base
personal-knowledge-base.content: A store of your own accumulated knowledge — notes, decisions, references — organized so an AI can search and use it. The difference from a pile of documents: structure and maintenance. Level 2 builds one as a wiki.

children.text: By 2027, half of business decisions will be AI-augmented or automated, according to [Gartner's Top Data & Analytics Predictions](https://www.gartner.com/en/newsroom/press-releases/2025-06-17-gartner-announces-top-data-and-analytics-predictions). Executives already lean on it for judgment calls. 60% use AI regularly to support decisions, per [Deloitte's 2026 Global Human Capital Trends](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/topics/talent/human-capital-trends/2026/decision-making-with-ai.html), and Deloitte cites Oracle research finding 72% of leaders say data overload and mistrust in their own numbers have stalled decisions outright.

This system takes a hard question you're facing, a hire, a pricing change, a build-vs-buy call, plus whatever evidence you can hand it, and produces a one-page memo with options, evidence, tradeoffs, assumptions, and a recommendation. Forcing every tradeoff onto the page before you [commit](#tooltip-commit) is what changes the decision.

Run it as a paste-in [prompt](#tooltip-prompt) for the decision in front of you, a saved [skill](#tooltip-skill) for whenever a hard call comes up, or a scheduled [agent](#tooltip-agent) that pulls in prior decisions for precedent.

Open your AI chat and have it interview you into a scope document. Done means a written scope naming the kinds of decisions this covers, the evidence you'll feed it, who reviews the memo, and how you want it to challenge your thinking instead of agreeing with it.

children.prompt: I want to build a system with my AI tool that turns a hard decision I'm facing into a structured memo before I decide. Ask me questions, one at a time, about what kinds of decisions I want this for, what evidence and context I'd feed it, who else needs to review the memo before I act, and how I want it to challenge my thinking instead of just agreeing with me. Then write it up as a scope document I can build from.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: the interview forces you to define what counts as evidence and who signs off before you're facing a live decision.

items: Where past decisions and precedent already live, a doc, email threads, or a decision log.
Who needs to see the memo before it's final, just you, a co-founder, or a board.
How much of the underlying data your AI tool can see directly versus what you paste in by hand.

children.text: Bring the scope document and gather any access it calls for. Common [connectors](#tooltip-tool-connectors) are your [knowledge base](#tooltip-personal-knowledge-base) ([Notion](#tooltip-notion), Confluence, Google Drive) for precedent, your comms tools ([Slack](#tooltip-slack), Gmail, Outlook) for gathering input, and your meeting notes (Zoom, Fathom, Otter) for prior discussion on the same topic. The paste-in version needs none.
**Create.** Build and test the system on the actual decision in front of you. The prompt below is one example; your scope document has the full version.

children.prompt:
Goal: Turn [the decision I'm facing, stated as a question] into a one-page decision memo with options, evidence, tradeoffs, and a recommendation.

Context: Here's the background: [paste relevant notes, data, past related decisions, constraints]. My default bias is [risk-averse / move fast / consensus-seeking] and I want you to counter that, not confirm it.

Rules:
- List at least 2 to 3 real options, not one option plus straw men.
- For each, state the evidence for and against, the key assumption it depends on, and what would have to be true for it to fail.
- Flag anything I said that isn't backed by evidence in what I gave you.
- End with a clear recommendation and the one thing that would change it.
- Output as a one-page memo with headers: Question, Options, Evidence, Tradeoffs, Recommendation, Risks.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: naming your own bias upfront and asking the [model](#tooltip-model) to counter it is what keeps the memo from confirming what you already wanted to do.

children.text: **Review.** Check the output against your scope. Real alternatives instead of straw men, evidence cited for each, a stated bias countered?
**Feedback.** Tell it exactly which correction to fold in, for example the options were too safe, and update the rules so the next memo doesn't repeat it.

items: Build a memo template per decision type, hiring, pricing, vendor.
Add a step where your AI tool argues the strongest case against your instinct.
Track what you decided against what happened, then feed the outcome back in.
Flag when a new decision resembles one you already made.

children.text: **Measure** with a [rubric](#tooltip-rubric). Have your AI chat turn the scope bar into pass/fail checks and a run log in one pass.

children.prompt: From my scope document, write a rubric for judging each decision memo, with 4 to 6 pass/fail checks. Then set up a simple run log I can keep in a doc or spreadsheet, with columns for date, decision, options considered, recommendation given, whether I followed it, and the outcome. Give me both in a format I can paste into my notes.
children.prompt_note: How this prompt works: pass/fail checks catch a memo that only restates your instinct, and the outcome column is what eventually tells you whether the recommendations were any good.

children.text: **Log** every run. Note the date, which rubric checks passed or failed, and what changed. A single miss is noise, and a repeated miss is an unwritten instruction.

**Make skills** from what the log shows. Once the rubric passes decisions straight, package the prompt and corrected rules into a skill, so runs start from your defaults. A repeated failure earns its own skill. [Claude](#tooltip-claude)'s skill-creator skill will interview you and write it, and a custom GPT does the same in [ChatGPT](#tooltip-chatgpt).
A memo that always agrees with your first instinct isn't [pushing](#tooltip-push) you anywhere. Check whether it ever argued back, and if it hasn't, fix the rules that let it stay quiet.
